text:
ops-bot: ALERT: ECC corrected error rate on gpu-card-7c for cluster-gamma > baseline (20/min) — 34 in last 3m. ticket: #INC-3482
liam: seeing the same series, routed here. stack trace? any Xid or kernel oops?
maya: quick dump attached in logs channel but tl;dr: corrected ECCs spike, no Xid yet. cards show rising corrected counts across 3 racks.
cheng: is this global or isolated to that HW batch? gpu-card-7c is a p4d-spot batch from last quarter, might be flaky silicon.
sre-jen: we need to decide soft-evac (move pods off) vs hard-retire. soft-evac buys us time but increases card churn.
liam: proposal: soft-evac when corrected errors > 25 in 5m OR corrected error rate slope > 50% vs 10m avg. hard-retire at 100 corrected or any uncorrectable/Xid.
katie: +1 but add a noise floor: ignore if job is synthetic or low-IO. also factor in recent memtest results.
maya: ops playbook snippet (rough):
```
# playbook excerpt: soft-evac policy
if corrected_errors(card, window=300s) >= 25:
  label node as "soft-evac-pending"
  schedule evacuation: migrate pods with non-strict affinity first
  start 30m observation timer
  if corrected_errors >= 100 or Xid_detected:
    escalate -> admin approval for hard-retire or immediate replacement
```
cheng: what about model-serving latency and batch windows? moving mid-inference could cause tail latency issues. we should prefer draining only low-priority pools first.
sre-jen: agree. add route-based policy: for gpu pools tagged "interactive" use higher threshold. for "batch" we can be aggressive.
liam: ops metric we should track: tokens/sec lost during evac, pod restart rate, and failed preempts. also track replacement cost estimate.
ops-bot: NOTE: recent change in kernel module 510.60 on nodes-gamma may change corrected ECC reporting frequency. check kernel-rollout history.
maya: I pulled kernel rollout: 2025-01-12 was applied to rack 7c -> matches start of spike. that suggests it's either driver sensitivity or cards coincidentally entering failure.
katie: can we do an immediate non-disruptive probe? run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` + `gpu-health-check --stress=30s --no-restart` on the node in readonly mode.
liam: running health probe now on one sample node (gpu-card-7c-01). output: corrected count climbed by 12 during 30s probe. suspicious.
cheng: that is a clear delta. next step: mark node for soft-evac and rotate a spare into that rack. avoid mass-evac until we confirm pattern.
sre-jen: ops runbook update items:
- thresholds: soft-evac >=25/5m OR slope>50%
- hard-retire: >=100/5m OR any uncorrectable/Xid/firmware ECC unfixable
- quarantine window: 30m observation after soft-evac before reintroducing
- fleet automation: if 3 distinct nodes in same HW batch hit soft-evac within 24h -> auto-scan batch and flag for replacement
- alert levels: P2 for soft-evac cluster events, P1 if Xid/uncorrectable seen

maya: automation note: avoid immediate fleet-wide drains — prefer staged pilot (1 node per rack) to reduce capacity shock.
liam: action items:
- @cheng run batch-scan for this HW lot and report by EOD
- @katie / @maya implement soft-evac label + probe command in fleetctl job template
- @sre-jen add thresholds to escalation playbook and update runbook page

katie: will add `fleetctl mark soft-evac` and a `fleetctl probe --readonly` job in CI. will also add metric for "evacuation-induced-restarts" to dashboard.
cheng: started batch-scan (ticket INC-3482-BATCH) — early results: 4/120 cards in same lot have transient corrected spikes but only 1 crossed 25/5m.
maya: given kernel rollout correlation, ops-run: roll back kernel on one pilot rack tonight and observe 6h. if corrected counts drop, file kernel regression with vendor.
liam: final thought — we should avoid hard rules that immediately OOO nodes without human review unless Xid/unrecoverable. soft-evac + 30m observation + automated batch heuristics seems balanced.
sre-jen: agreed. logging this thread into runbook PR after action items done.
ops-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: INC-3482 "gpu ecc spike - soft-evac policy discussion" — initial P2.
katie: thanks team. I'll start the fleet changes now and ping when CI job merged.
liam: thanks. I'll monitor the alert channel and escalate if Xid pops up.
